items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: And then the guys are always filling in like Manuel Paul or Louis Nelson.

ctx.x: But of course, and it's taken for granted, he'll be playing when the clarinet player drops out. Like the Thomas band, Thomas plays the straightest lead of anybody in town. More so than a person, anybody. Short, hot notes. With the biggest gaping holes. And then the guys are always filling in like Manuel Paul or Louis Nelson. But a clarinet player, the silence angle is extremely important because he's got to drop out so there's room for the other men. So you have the band sound rather than just a bunch of…
But this goes back to the conception of discipline and form.
